correctness.rationale: The branch recursion is L_{n+1} =d Z+log(1+exp L_n) with independent inputs. For a positive shift, the density ratio f(x-u)/f(x) is strictly increasing by strict concavity of log f, establishing the base case. For the inductive step, an increasing bijection onto the transformed support preserves the density-ratio inequality. Splitting the determinant of the two convolution densities into u<v and u>v gives over u<v the product of the strictly positive translation-kernel determinant and the strictly positive ordered input-density determinant. The positive bounded increment density and probability inputs justify these integrations. For adjacent sites, independence of the two branches and the isolated edge, and pairing Y with 1/Y, give the antisymmetric kernel of lines 34–39. On u<v that kernel has positive sign for Y≠1 and the density difference has the same sign. The expectation is well-defined since the starting difference is between two normalized probabilities. The branch of length zero is deterministic 1, the equal-length center cancels, and reversing and negating all iid symmetric increments proves reflection. Scaling nondegenerate disorder by any finite β>0 preserves the hypotheses; the β=0 case is uniform. This is only the restricted classical single-wall law. Gaussian quadrature checks were inspected but not used as proof or rerun.

value.rationale: It turns a known experimental/asymptotic physical bias into a strict, site-by-site order, including intermediate temperatures and non-Gaussian log-concave disorder. The proof provides a useful mechanism for why the order persists after quenched normalization. It neither extrapolates a sampled U shape nor merely imports the limiting arcsine law.
